positioning: Kubernetes v1.33 focuses on Native Sidecar Containers, Checkpoint/Restore & Node Lifecycle, API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale, and In-Place Pod Vertical Scaling. For operators, this release translates 261 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.

high_level_changes.headline: Native Sidecar Containers, Checkpoint/Restore & Node Lifecycle
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves native sidecar containers, checkpoint/restore & node lifecycle for service-mesh pods, telemetry agents, fast-restoring stateful apps, and oci artifact mounts running on kubelet cri runtime (containerd / cri-o) and linux/windows worker nodes, delivering stops zombie sidecars from holding batch nodes open after job completion.

high_level_changes.headline: API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves api server & etcd watch/cache efficiency at scale for operator-heavy platforms, argo cd / flux gitops controllers, and multi-tenant clusters with 10k+ crds/pods running on control plane (`kube-apiserver`, `etcd`, `kube-controller-manager`) cpu and memory footprint, delivering cuts control-plane memory spikes by 30–50% during list storms and prevents cascading `etcd` overload outages.

high_level_changes.headline: In-Place Pod Vertical Scaling
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves in-place pod vertical scaling for stateful microservices, warm inference engines, jvms, and suspended batch jobs needing cpu/ram adjustments running on linux worker nodes and kubelet resource allocation loops, delivering eliminates over-provisioning buffer and avoids expensive pod restart cold-starts during traffic spikes.

high_level_changes.headline: Feature Enhancements
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves feature enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.

high_level_changes.headline: CEL-Based Validating & Mutating Admission Policies
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves cel-based validating & mutating admission policies for platform security guardrails, multi-tenant compliance policies, and default resource injectors running on in-process `kube-apiserver` admission chain (replaces external webhook deployments), delivering removes dedicated webhook pods and eliminates deployment outages caused by webhook timeouts.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Kubernetes' next-generation API (`resource.k8s.io`) for requesting, sharing, and topology-aligning specialized hardware like GPUs, TPUs, and NICs—replacing rigid integer device plugins.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Lets multiple pods share fractional GPUs safely or co-schedule across NVLink domains without custom vendor hacks.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Changing a running Pod's CPU or memory requests/limits dynamically without killing and recreating the container.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Eliminates cold-start restarts and dropped connections when scaling stateful services, databases, or warm AI model servers.

jargon_glossary.meaning: First-class lifecycle support for helper containers (log shippers, service mesh proxies) so they start before the main app and terminate automatically after Batch Jobs finish.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Fixes the classic Kubernetes bug where a finished Job hangs forever because an Istio/Envoy sidecar stays alive.

jargon_glossary.meaning: In-process policy rules written in Common Expression Language (CEL) evaluated directly inside `kube-apiserver` without calling external admission webhook servers.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Removes webhook network latency and prevents a crashed policy pod from taking down cluster deployments.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Maps the `root` user inside a container to an unprivileged non-root UID on the host node kernel.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Dramatically reduces container-escape blast radius even for legacy workloads that require running as `root` inside the container.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Streaming object lists from `kube-apiserver` memory cache snapshots instead of assembling giant one-shot payloads from `etcd`.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Slashes API server RAM spikes and protects `etcd` from OOM crashes during controller restarts on large clusters.

jargon_glossary.meaning: A modern Linux kernel packet-filtering backend for Kubernetes Service routing that replaces legacy `iptables` linear rule chains.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Cuts Service rule programming latency and CPU overhead on clusters with tens of thousands of Services.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Allows `HorizontalPodAutoscaler` to scale external/queue-driven workloads all the way down to 0 replicas when idle and wake them when queue depth rises.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Directly cuts cloud compute and GPU bills for bursty batch/inference workers during off-peak hours.

jargon_glossary.meaning: The standard plugin layer connecting Kubernetes PersistentVolumes to cloud block/file storage providers.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Controls how fast stateful workloads attach disks, recover from node failures, and handle credentials.

should_i_upgrade.text: Added the ability to reduce both the initial delay and the maximum delay accrued between container restarts for a node for containers in `CrashLoopBackOff` across the cluster to the recommended values of `1s` initial delay and `60s` maximum delay. To set this for a node, turn on the feature gate `ReduceDefaultCrashLoopBackOffDecay`. If you are also using the feature gate `KubeletCrashLoopBackOffMax` with a configured per-node `CrashLoopBackOff.MaxContainerRestartPeriod`, the effective kubelet configuration will follow the conflict resolution policy described further in the documentation [here](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle/#reduced-container-restart-delay). ([#130711](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/130711), [@lauralorenz](https://github.com/lauralorenz)) [SIG Node and Testing]

[Action Required] CSI drivers that call IsLikelyNotMountPoint should not assume false means that the path is a mount point. Each CSI driver needs to make sure correct usage of return value of IsLikelyNotMountPoint because if the file is an irregular file but not a mount point is acceptable ([#129370](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/129370), [@andyzhangx](https://github.com/andyzhangx)) [SIG Storage and Windows]

Fixed the behavior of the `KUBE_PROXY_NFTABLES_SKIP_KERNEL_VERSION_CHECK` environment variable in the nftables proxier. The kernel version check is now skipped only when this variable is explicitly set to a non-empty value. To skip the check, set the `KUBE_PROXY_NFTABLES_SKIP_KERNEL_VERSION_CHECK` environment variable. ([#130401](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/130401), [@ryota-sakamoto](https://github.com/ryota-sakamoto))

Renamed `UpdatePodTolerations` action type to `UpdatePodToleration`. Action required for custom plugin developers to update their code to follow the rename. ([#129023](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/129023), [@zhifei92](https://github.com/zhifei92)) [SIG Scheduling and Testing]

The EndpointSlice `hints` field has graduated to GA. The beta annotation `service.kubernetes.io/topology-mode` is now considered deprecated and will not graduate to GA. It remains operational for backward compatibility. Users are encouraged to use the `spec.trafficDistribution` field in the Service API for topology-aware routing configuration. ([#130742](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/130742), [@gauravkghildiyal](https://github.com/gauravkghildiyal)) [SIG Network]

The `StorageCapacityScoring` feature gate was added to score nodes by available storage capacity. It's in alpha and disabled by default. The `VolumeCapacityPriority` alpha feature was replaced with this, and the default behavior was changed. The `VolumeCapacityPriority` preferred a node with the least allocatable, but the `StorageCapacityScoring` preferred a node with the maximum allocatable. See [KEP-4049](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-storage/4049-storage-capacity-scoring-of-nodes-for-dynamic-provisioning/README.md) for details. ([#128184](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/128184), [@cupnes](https://github.com/cupnes)) [SIG Scheduling, Storage and Testing]

The `WatchFromStorageWithoutResourceVersion` feature was deprecated and can no longer be enabled. ([#129930](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/129930), [@serathius](https://github.com/serathius))

The pod `status.resize` field is now deprecated and will no longer be set. The status of a pod resize will be exposed under two new conditions: `PodResizeInProgress` and `PodResizePending` instead. ([#130733](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/130733), [@natasha41575](https://github.com/natasha41575)) [SIG API Machinery, Apps, CLI, Node, Scheduling and Testing]
sigs: API Machinery, Apps, CLI, Node, Scheduling and Testing

wheres_the_proof.text: Graduated the `MultiCIDRServiceAllocator` feature gate to stable, and the `DisableAllocatorDualWrite` feature gate to beta (disabled by default). **Action required** for Kubernetes cluster administrators and for distributions that manage the cluster Service CIDR. Kubernetes now allows users to define the cluster Service CIDR via an API object: ServiceCIDR. Distributions or administrators of Kubernetes may want to control that new Service CIDRs added to the cluster do not overlap with other networks on the cluster, that only belong to a specific range of IPs. Administrators may also prefer to retain the existing behavior of only having one ServiceCIDR per cluster. You can use `ValidatingAdmissionPolicy` to achieve this. ([#128971](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/128971), [@aojea](https://github.com/aojea)) [SIG Apps, Architecture, Auth, CLI, Etcd, Network, Release and Testing]
sigs: Apps, Architecture, Auth, CLI, Etcd, Network, Release and Testing

wheres_the_proof.text: The `SidecarContainers` feature has graduated to GA. 'SidecarContainers' feature gate was locked to default value and will be removed in v1.36. If you were setting this feature gate explicitly, please remove it now. ([#129731](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/129731), [@gjkim42](https://github.com/gjkim42)) [SIG Apps, Node, Scheduling and Testing]

Promoted in-place Pod vertical scaling to beta. The `InPlacePodVerticalScaling` feature gate is now enabled by default. ([#130905](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/130905), [@tallclair](https://github.com/tallclair)) [SIG Node]

The `RemoteRequestHeaderUID` feature moves to beta and is now enabled by default. This makes the kube-apiserver propagate UIDs in the `X-Remote-Uid` header in requests to the aggregated API servers. The header is not honored by default for incoming requests, but that can be enabled by setting the `--requestheader-uid-headers` flag explicitly. ([#130560](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/130560), [@stlaz](https://github.com/stlaz)) [SIG API Machinery, Auth and Testing]

Graduated the `DisableNodeKubeProxyVersion` feature gate to enable by default, the kubelet no longer attempts to set the `.status.kubeProxyVersion` field for its associated Node. ([#129713](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/129713), [@HirazawaUi](https://github.com/HirazawaUi)) [SIG Node]

kubeadm: removed the feature gate EtcdLearnerMode which graduated to GA in 1.32. ([#129589](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/129589), [@neolit123](https://github.com/neolit123)) [SIG Cluster Lifecycle]

KEP-3619: fine-grained supplemental groups policy is graduated to Beta. Note that kubelet now rejects pods with `.spec.securityContext.supplementalGroupsPolicy: Strict` when scheduled to the node that does not support the feature (`.status.features.supplementalGroupsPolicy: false`). ([#130210](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/130210), [@everpeace](https://github.com/everpeace)) [SIG Apps, Node and Testing]

Kubernetes components that accepted X.509 client certificate authentication now read the user UID from a certificate subject name RDN with object ID `1.3.6.1.4.1.57683.2`. An RDN with this object ID had to contain a string value and appear no more than once in the certificate subject. Reading the user UID from this RDN could be disabled by setting the beta feature gate `AllowParsingUserUIDFromCertAuth` to `false`(until the feature gate graduated to GA). ([#127897](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/127897), [@modulitos](https://github.com/modulitos)) [SIG API Machinery, Auth and Testing]

Promoted the Job's `JobBackoffLimitPerIndex` feature-gate to stable. ([#130061](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/130061), [@mimowo](https://github.com/mimowo)) [SIG API Machinery, Apps, Architecture and Testing]

# What's New in Kubernetes v1.33

## High-Level Explanation
Kubernetes v1.33 focuses on Native Sidecar Containers, Checkpoint/Restore & Node Lifecycle, API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale, and In-Place Pod Vertical Scaling. For operators, this release translates 261 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.

## 1. What Are the High-Level Changes?
- **Native Sidecar Containers, Checkpoint/Restore & Node Lifecycle**: Improves native sidecar containers, checkpoint/restore & node lifecycle for service-mesh pods, telemetry agents, fast-restoring stateful apps, and oci artifact mounts running on kubelet cri runtime (containerd / cri-o) and linux/windows worker nodes, delivering stops zombie sidecars from holding batch nodes open after job completion.
- **API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale**: Improves api server & etcd watch/cache efficiency at scale for operator-heavy platforms, argo cd / flux gitops controllers, and multi-tenant clusters with 10k+ crds/pods running on control plane (`kube-apiserver`, `etcd`, `kube-controller-manager`) cpu and memory footprint, delivering cuts control-plane memory spikes by 30–50% during list storms and prevents cascading `etcd` overload outages.
- **In-Place Pod Vertical Scaling**: Improves in-place pod vertical scaling for stateful microservices, warm inference engines, jvms, and suspended batch jobs needing cpu/ram adjustments running on linux worker nodes and kubelet resource allocation loops, delivering eliminates over-provisioning buffer and avoids expensive pod restart cold-starts during traffic spikes.
- **Feature Enhancements**: Improves feature enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.
- **CEL-Based Validating & Mutating Admission Policies**: Improves cel-based validating & mutating admission policies for platform security guardrails, multi-tenant compliance policies, and default resource injectors running on in-process `kube-apiserver` admission chain (replaces external webhook deployments), delivering removes dedicated webhook pods and eliminates deployment outages caused by webhook timeouts.

## 2. Who Benefits? (Models, GPUs & Your Bill)

|---|---|---|---|
| **Native Sidecar Containers, Checkpoint/Restore & Node Lifecycle** | Service-mesh pods, telemetry agents, fast-restoring stateful apps, and OCI artifact mounts | Kubelet CRI runtime (containerd / CRI-O) and Linux/Windows worker nodes | Stops zombie sidecars from holding batch nodes open after job completion |
| **API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale** | Operator-heavy platforms, Argo CD / Flux GitOps controllers, and multi-tenant clusters with 10k+ CRDs/Pods | Control plane (`kube-apiserver`, `etcd`, `kube-controller-manager`) CPU and memory footprint | Cuts control-plane memory spikes by 30–50% during list storms and prevents cascading `etcd` overload outages |
| **In-Place Pod Vertical Scaling (Zero-Restart Resource Resize)** | Stateful microservices, warm inference engines, JVMs, and suspended Batch Jobs needing CPU/RAM adjustments | Linux worker nodes and kubelet resource allocation loops | Eliminates over-provisioning buffer and avoids expensive pod restart cold-starts during traffic spikes |
| **Feature Enhancements** | General platform workloads and API consumers | Standard cluster nodes and runtime components | Operational reliability and lower maintenance toil |
| **CEL-Based Validating & Mutating Admission Policies** | Platform security guardrails, multi-tenant compliance policies, and default resource injectors | In-process `kube-apiserver` admission chain (replaces external webhook deployments) | Removes dedicated webhook pods and eliminates deployment outages caused by webhook timeouts |
| **Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) & GPU/Accelerator Management** | AI/ML training, LLM inference pods, fractional/multi-GPU workloads, and NIC/FPGA consumers | NVIDIA/AMD GPU nodes, multi-NIC RDMA clusters, and topology-aware hardware pools | Higher GPU utilization and fewer stranded accelerators via standardized device sharing and health reporting |
| **API Change Enhancements** | General platform workloads and API consumers | Standard cluster nodes and runtime components | Operational reliability and lower maintenance toil |

## 3. What Does the Jargon Mean?
- **DRA (Dynamic Resource Allocation)**: Kubernetes' next-generation API (`resource.k8s.io`) for requesting, sharing, and topology-aligning specialized hardware like GPUs, TPUs, and NICs—replacing rigid integer device plugins. Why it matters: Lets multiple pods share fractional GPUs safely or co-schedule across NVLink domains without custom vendor hacks.
- **In-Place Pod Vertical Scaling (Resize)**: Changing a running Pod's CPU or memory requests/limits dynamically without killing and recreating the container. Why it matters: Eliminates cold-start restarts and dropped connections when scaling stateful services, databases, or warm AI model servers.
- **Native Sidecar Containers (`initContainers` with `restartPolicy: Always`)**: First-class lifecycle support for helper containers (log shippers, service mesh proxies) so they start before the main app and terminate automatically after Batch Jobs finish. Why it matters: Fixes the classic Kubernetes bug where a finished Job hangs forever because an Istio/Envoy sidecar stays alive.
- **ValidatingAdmissionPolicy & MutatingAdmissionPolicy (CEL)**: In-process policy rules written in Common Expression Language (CEL) evaluated directly inside `kube-apiserver` without calling external admission webhook servers. Why it matters: Removes webhook network latency and prevents a crashed policy pod from taking down cluster deployments.
- **Linux User Namespaces (`hostUsers: false`)**: Maps the `root` user inside a container to an unprivileged non-root UID on the host node kernel. Why it matters: Dramatically reduces container-escape blast radius even for legacy workloads that require running as `root` inside the container.
- **WatchList & Snapshottable Watch Cache**: Streaming object lists from `kube-apiserver` memory cache snapshots instead of assembling giant one-shot payloads from `etcd`. Why it matters: Slashes API server RAM spikes and protects `etcd` from OOM crashes during controller restarts on large clusters.
- **nftables `kube-proxy` Backend**: A modern Linux kernel packet-filtering backend for Kubernetes Service routing that replaces legacy `iptables` linear rule chains. Why it matters: Cuts Service rule programming latency and CPU overhead on clusters with tens of thousands of Services.
- **HPA Scale-to-Zero (`minReplicas: 0`)**: Allows `HorizontalPodAutoscaler` to scale external/queue-driven workloads all the way down to 0 replicas when idle and wake them when queue depth rises. Why it matters: Directly cuts cloud compute and GPU bills for bursty batch/inference workers during off-peak hours.
- **CSI (Container Storage Interface)**: The standard plugin layer connecting Kubernetes PersistentVolumes to cloud block/file storage providers. Why it matters: Controls how fast stateful workloads attach disks, recover from node failures, and handle credentials.
